summary: The geometry meets every graded number: lengths 44/25/21, flexion sweeps clear, channels 2.2 mm, FEA SF > 3, no overhangs, and the lap-knuckle side-print scheme is clever and printable. But no joint has an extension stop. Measured on assembly.step, every joint bends backward freely to about -60 deg, so pulling the extensor does not 'straighten' the finger; it bends it backward. The pivots are also fully threaded M3 screws turning in printed bores under tendon loads about 20x the FEA case.

findings.issue: No hyperextension (straight) hard stop at any joint. Child positioned at negative flexion against its parent in assembly.step: intersection volume is zero at -10, -30 and -45 deg, 0.09 mm3 at -60 deg, and 13.6 mm3 only at -70 deg (same for mcp, pip and dip). The pocket rect |x-lj| <= XT removes all parent material in the child's band, and child_end keeps nothing behind the axis outside RH. So the extensor (or the elastic the DESIGN recommends on it) pulls each joint backward until something at about -60 deg stops it. With 3 joints and 2 tendons the straight pose is not defined by line lengths: it only exists if each joint bottoms out on a stop at 0 deg. A push on the back of the finger also folds it backward. This fails the brief's 'straightens when the lines are pulled'. The sweeps only test [0, range], so no check catches it.
findings.fix: Add a dorsal extension stop at every joint that makes contact at 0 deg (0 to -2 deg), e.g. a dorsal lug on the child's non-knuckle band that sits behind the axis and bears on a matching dorsal shoulder of the parent's knuckle band (shrink RK or the pocket there, or let the lug stand just proud of the dorsal surface). Prove it: sweep each joint to -5 deg and require contact, while keeping [0, range] clear. Make the engine general too: a revolute joint should be able to declare a hard stop that the sweep proves (collides just outside the range).

findings.issue: The pivots are ISO 4762 M3 x 14 SHCS, which are fully threaded at that length (b = 18 mm). The moving part therefore turns on thread crests in a 3.35 mm printed PETG bore for 7.85 mm. The real pivot load is set by the tendon, not by the 15 N FEA case: DESIGN s7 gives flexor tension = 22.5 x tip force at the mcp (about 225-340 N for a 10-15 N tip force). That is about 10-14 MPa of projected bearing on threads, cycling, so the bore wears oval and the finger gets sloppy quickly. kerf itself warns on all three pin groups to 'use a shoulder screw'. DESIGN s8 states pin bearing as 0.64 MPa from the 15 N case only, which understates it 15-20x.
findings.fix: Turn on a smooth surface: an ISO 7379 shoulder screw (4 mm shoulder, M3 thread, bore 4.35), or a 3 mm steel dowel/brass tube bushing pressed into the child with the M3 screw through it. Add a catalog entry with its source. Redo the pin bearing hand-check with the tendon reaction (tip force + flexor tension vector) and state it in DESIGN s8.

findings.issue: Over the top ~1 mm of the heat-set bore (the gap face), the swept extensor groove comes to r ~ 2.5 mm from the pivot axis. Measured: a ring r 2.05-3.0 at the gap face is only 96 % solid on base/proximal. The CNC Kitchen insert knurl is D1 4.6 (r 2.3), so the wall is ~0.2 mm against a catalog min wall of 1.6. Plastic the hot insert pushes aside will flow into the extensor groove and leave a lip in the 0.3 mm lap gap.
findings.fix: Recess the insert 0.3-0.5 mm below the gap face (bore counterbore) and/or move the extensor crown points out (EXT 5 -> 5.5 to 6 with the wrap angle) so the swept groove stays >= 1.6 mm from the insert OD; or use the M3 short insert (L 3.0) set deeper.

findings.issue: The knuckle-face tendon grooves are a union of straight tubes at 10 deg steps. The part renders (proximal/base/distal top views) show a serrated fan of ridges that the braided line rides across as the joint turns. Under 200+ N of flexor tension those ridges abrade the line and the plastic.
findings.fix: Sample at 2-3 deg, or build the groove as one swept/lofted solid, so the fan floor is smooth.

findings.issue: Line termination: 3 mm knot pockets behind a 2.2 mm channel. A single stopper knot in 0.5 mm braid is ~1.5-2 mm and can pull into the channel, so retention rests mostly on CA glue. At straight-finger tip loads the flexor carries 5-11x the tip force here.
findings.fix: Specify a crimp sleeve or bead larger than 2.5 mm (or a double figure-eight), or add a cross-pin/transverse wrap post in the distal so the line does not depend on the glue.

findings.issue: The flexor moment arm is only 4 mm (inside the 7.5 mm knuckle disc), so tendon tension is 22.5x the tip force at a straight finger. The 445 N line rates ~10 N tip force at SF 2, and the actuator and pivots see the full tension. Documented in DESIGN, but it drives the pivot wear above.
findings.fix: If a larger grip force is wanted, route the flexor palmar of the knuckle (a pulley/sheath at r ~ 6-7 mm) to halve the tension. Otherwise state the tip-force rating in the README/ASSEMBLY.

findings.issue: The screw heads (5.5 dia x 3 mm, on alternating sides) are not modelled as proxies, so they are not in any collision or envelope check. The real finger is ~22 mm wide at the knuckles, against 16 mm for the parts, and a neighbouring finger in a hand will rub the heads.
findings.fix: Add the screws as catalog proxies so the sweeps include the heads, or use a low-head (ISO 7380 / DIN 7984) screw or counterbore the heads into the outer faces, and note the spacing to adjacent fingers.

findings.issue: Wall check warns of 1.14-1.15 mm walls (below the 1.2 mm reliable minimum), at the tendon grooves and knot pockets.
findings.fix: Shift the knot pockets or channel 0.1-0.2 mm, or narrow the groove locally, to get >= 1.2 mm.

findings.issue: The FEA follows the brief's load case: hot spots at the pip load bore and the mcp fixed bore, where expected, with peak 12.4 MPa against a 24 MPa allowable and 0.34 mm deflection. But it omits the flexor compression, which is the dominant real load (axial ~20x tip force plus bearing at both bores).
findings.fix: Add a second load case with the tendon reaction at both pivots, so the pivot-bore bearing at the real load is shown.
